characterList.description: Man wearing black suit, white shirt and black tie with glasses. Holding a black microphone
characterList.name: Kyle Platt

characterList.description: Woman wearing pink shirt, glasses and pearl necklace
characterList.name: Marianne Copenhagenhaver

content_metadata.description: An interview with Marianne Copenhagenhaver discussing politics within the Libertarian movement, her activities, and experiences.

qAndA.answer: She is drinking a Starbucks iced coffee.
qAndA.question: What is Marianne drinking?

qAndA.answer: They are in a large hotel lobby with a balcony overlooking the lower level.
qAndA.question: What type of building are Marianne and Kyle in?

qAndA.answer: By emphasizing her diverse range of work, Kyle aims to portray Marianne as a highly motivated and dedicated individual, especially in contrast to her online persona as 'Libertarian Girl,' which might imply a more limited focus.
qAndA.question: Why does Kyle repeatedly refer to the fact that very few people know about Marianne's other activities?

qAndA.answer: She mentions Justin Amash, a Republican Congressman who openly identifies as a Libertarian, as an example of how working within the party can influence others towards Libertarian ideas.
qAndA.question: What specific event does Marianne reference when explaining her reasoning for working within the Republican party?

qAndA.answer: Kyle starts with a lighthearted and playful tone, making jokes about Marianne's busy schedule. However, he shifts to a more serious and thoughtful demeanor as he delves into the contentious topics of politics and Marianne's experience with accusations. His tone becomes increasingly supportive and encouraging towards the end, highlighting her passion and dedication to freedom.
qAndA.question: How does Kyle's tone change throughout the interview?

Well, I think that that's the best way to reach out to people because if you have major

Sure, sure.
So you're saying that it's important as a tool to spread ideas.
Not necessarily.
You aren't claiming that it's some pure libertarian ideology to engage in partisan or electoral
politics.
But the fact of the matter is most of us are here because of Ron Paul.
A lot of us are here because of Ron Paul.
And so that works.
Is that an accurate depiction?
Yes.
I don't believe it's working on the federal level is very productive because I think that
it's so far gone that there's not much that you can do on a federal level.
On the local level, however, I think you can do a lot.
You can stop tax increases and you can stop regulatory zoning issues, stuff like that.
And everything, every little bit helps.
So I think that's really important to start the groundwork from the local level to the
federal level.
Sure.
But even on the federal level, we use the or he used the Republican debates as Ron Paul did

On the federal level?
I don't know.
I would say like events like what's going on right now, you've got Justin Amash down

himself as a libertarian.
And I think that encourages other congressmen to get out and do the same.
And he has said that that inspires them and a lot of them run for office because of
him.
So I think that that's an amazing thing.
I don't think that there's anything negative about the word libertarian being used in
the government on a federal level.
Some people have accused you of being a shill for the Republican Party and different things

I want to know because I've never asked you, what is it that makes you, I mean there

for as many people as possible?

I'm sorry.

It's always a pleasure.

youtube_description:
Kyle Platt chats with Marianne Copenhaver (Libertarian Girl) at the International Students For Liberty Conference 2014 about the arduous task of growing libertarianism in the shell of the Republican Party.

Marianne gives her suggestions on how you as an individual can help expand your own personal freedom.

Join the liberty expanding discussion at Liberty.me: http://liberty.me/discuss/topics/philosophy-economic-theory/
